newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong, China coffee firms absorb price surge.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong, China coffee firms absorb price surge.

text.p: Coffee manufacturers in Hong Kong and China said on Friday their prices would remain unaffected in the short term but if coffee kept climbing, they would be forced to take measures.
Pacific Coffee Co Ltd, a major importer of Arabica coffee beans in Hong Kong planned to absorb the hike in prices for the next couple of months, a manager told Reuters.

"We are in a position right now where we are taking it on board, no customer of ours will be feeling the price rise for the next quarter," said Denis Riley, manager of marketing and business development.
LIFFE coffee opened sharply up on Friday after a dizzy New York rally on Thursday, with July soaring to a $2,055 life of contract high at 0918 GMT.
Riley said if the climb continued the company would be forced to reconsider its pricing policy.
"We're buying coffee out of the world market, we're roasting it and air-freighting it out here, we're very close to that market. That market flinches, we feel it," he said.
Pacific Coffee pioneered the gourmet coffee business in Hong Kong four years ago and is one of British colony's top three gourmet coffee providers, Riley said.
"In terms of gourmet coffee, we are the biggest importers of Arabica coffee beans in Hong Kong," he said.
A source at a major international coffee manufacturer in China said that the rise in coffee prices would not affect the firm's business.
"We have already prepared for that, since coffee is a very important ingredient for our business," said a Beijing-based company source who requested anonymity.

"We do not anticipate any impact for the rest of this year," he said, but noted that should the price hike continue beyond 1997, the company may have to increase its coffee prices or take other measures to protect its profitability.
